== Biography ==
James Glasgow was born on 23 March 1823.
<ref name="a">Family records known by [[Zehnder-8|Amy]]</ref>
<ref name="f"/>
<ref>Based on age 67 at death 1903; or age 75 in the 1901 census.</ref>
His father was named Samuel Glasgow.
<ref name="m2"/>

He came to New York from Cookstown, County Tyrone as a young man. He was a ferry boat captain in New York harbor working for Cornelius Vanderbilt. 
<ref name="a"/>

On 1 January 1864 in Manhattan, he married Jane McGowan, who was originally from Ireland as well.
<ref name="a"/>
<ref>"New York, New York City Marriage Records, 1829-1940," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:248M-LRT : 10 February 2018), James Glargow and Jane Mcgowan, 01 Jan 1864; citing Marriage, Manhattan, New York, New York, United States, New York City Municipal Archives, New York; FHL microfilm 1,671,674.</ref>

They returned to Cookstown, however Jane passed away in childbirth in 1866 with their first child. James remained in Ireland; turning down an offer by Vanderbilt to go into railroads. What that offer was is unknown, but they may have needed engineers. 
<ref name="a"/>

On 25 March 1873 at Oritor Presbyterian, he married Mary Jane Hopper of Drumshanbo, daughter of James Hopper, farmer. Witnessed by Samuel Glasgow Crawford and James Hopper.
<ref name="m2">[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/2e4b7b2808773 James Glasgow, Mary Jane Hopper, 1873, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages</ref> They settled at Gortin, Cookstown to raise a family.

He passed away 27 Jan 1903, widower, age 67, at Gortin, due to bronchitis. Informed by Lizzie Glasgow, daughter.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/2725364613523 James Glasgow, 1903, Cookstown, 67] at Irish Civil Registration - Deaths</ref>
James and Mary are buried at Kildress Church of Ireland churchyard.
<ref name="f">[[Space:Kildress_Church_of_Ireland_Churchyard%2C_Cookstown%2C_Tyrone]]; {{FindAGrave|229951843}} - note incorrect death year on Findagrave profile</ref>
The chief mourners were:
<ref>[https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0002006/19030131/058/0005 "Funeral of Mr. James Glasgow, Gortin"], ''Mid-Ulster Mail'' - Saturday 31 January 1903, Page 5</ref>
* Richard Glasgow, [[Glasgow-2051|Willie George Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-2050|Silas Glasgow]] (sons)
* [[Hopper-4318|James Hopper]], [[Hopper-4317|Andrew Hopper]] (brothers-in-law)
* [[Craig-12757|G. Craig]] (nephew)
A marriage for James Glasgow and Happer was registered on 25 March 1873 in the Cookstown district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 25 March 1873, Cookstown district, M/1873/L1/1132/1/191.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2054]] is assessed at 94% (proved). James’s 25 March 1873 Cookstown marriage names Samuel Glasgow as father, and the 1843 Gortin confirmation plus farm succession support the selected local man. The 1823 family birth,1901 age 75 and 1903 death age 67 disagree without negating that paternal identification.

Selected father-profile identity and paternal relationship; maternal identity is separate.

Next useful test: Compare original 1864 New York and 1873 Irish parent fields.

Source basis already held: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/2e4b7b2808773 On 25 March 1873 at Oritor Presbyterian, he married Mary Jane Hopper of Drumshanbo, daughter of James Hopper, farmer. Witnessed by Samuel Glasgow Crawford and James Hopper.  James Glasgow, Mary Jane Hopper, 1873, Cookstown (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/2e4b7b2808773) at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


A newspaper photo, [[Space:Eight_Brothers_and_Sisters_Together_After_30_years|Eight Brothers and Sisters Together After 30 years]], shows some of James's children: Silas, Robert, Thomas, William, Henry, Eleanor/Elizabeth, Sarah, and Mary. 

"Henry" seems likely to be the 1876 unnamed birth registration to this couple.

Perhaps therefore "Richard" whose name appears on the obituary as a son, is the 1875 unnamed birth record. However, ancestry-com public trees name the 1875 record as a "Samuel" dies 1902, although no firm sources are given to corroborate that.

On the 1910 US census, son Henry has an Aunt called Sarah E. Wallace, widow, born abt. 1825 Ireland.  Not sure if this was James's sister, or sister-in-law. There are records for a Sarah Glasgow m. William Wallace in Ohio moving to Michigan, but she dies in 1908 and so could not be the same aunt from the 1910 census.

In the Derryloran parish register, James Glasgow of Gortin is Confirmed at age 21 in 1843. This could perhaps tell us that his birth year was 1822 rather than 1823.
<ref>[[Space:The_Parish_Registers_of_Derryloran_parish_church|The Parish Registers of Derryloran parish church]] - Vol2.</ref>
